# Smokescreen

> Smoke for Bevy 0.20 games that fills rooms, pours through doorways, stops at walls and blocks sight, with line-of-sight queries that agree with what players see. `bevy_smokescreen` is the Bevy plugin: it draws the smoke and adds components, messages and queries. `smokescreen` is the simulation underneath, with no engine in it and the same answers bit for bit on every machine, for dedicated servers, bots and other engines.

This file maps the API of `bevy_smokescreen` and `smokescreen` 0.2 for coding assistants, with recipes. Its Rust code is compiled against 0.2 as doc tests. Each published version of `bevy_smokescreen` carries its own copy at the root of its package.

- **Which crate.** A Bevy game depends on `bevy_smokescreen`, which re-exports the core as `bevy_smokescreen::smokescreen`. A headless server, bots or another engine depend on `smokescreen` alone (Rust 1.88 or newer; it depends only on `glam` and `libm`). In a workspace with both, `smokescreen = "0.2"` resolves to the version the plugin pins.
- **Versions.** `bevy_smokescreen` 0.2 is for Bevy 0.20 only, and needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer.
- **Imports.** `use bevy::prelude::*;` and `use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;` cover most code. `Config`, `Tuning`, `CloudSpec`, `CloudSource`, `CloudId`, `Smokes`, `Level`, `SmokeTimeline` and `HoleSettings` are at the plugin's root (`bevy_smokescreen::Config`), not in the prelude. For the core alone: `use smokescreen::*;` and `use smokescreen::glam::Vec3;` (the same `Vec3` as Bevy's).
- **Units.** Positions, lengths and volumes are in your world's units: Y-up metres unless you choose others (recipe "Your own units").
- **Rules and looks.** What hides what (the rules) must be the same on every machine in a match: the `Tuning` in the plugin's `Config`, the level, and each smoke's style, volume, lifetime, grow time, seed and source. The look may differ from machine to machine: `SmokeSettings`, a smoke's tint and density, each camera's quality dial.
- **Ticks.** The simulation runs on ticks (`Config::tick_rate`: 128 a second in the plugin by default), counted from Bevy's virtual time unless you drive `SmokeClock` yourself. A `Smoke` pops, and bullets and explosions land, on the current tick.
- **GPU.** Volumetric and faceted smoke need compute shaders: native (Vulkan, Metal, DX12) or WebGPU. On WebGL2 the game keeps running with crystal smoke only.
- **Setup mistakes** are logged once each, with the fix ("Warnings the plugin logs" below).
- **Not API.** Items hidden from the docs on docs.rs may change in any release: `CloudState`, `CloudView`, `View::clouds`, `Smokes::internal_tuning`, what a `CloudShape` holds, and the core's `grid`, `light` and `math` modules. Don't use them.

## Setup

```toml
[dependencies]
bevy = "0.20"
bevy_smokescreen = "0.2"
```

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        // After DefaultPlugins: the plugin needs Bevy's asset and render plugins.
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_systems(Startup, setup)
        .run();
}

fn setup(mut commands: Commands, mut meshes: ResMut<Assets<Mesh>>, mut materials: ResMut<Assets<StandardMaterial>>) {
    // Volumetric and faceted smoke are drawn only through cameras with SmokeCamera.
    commands.spawn((
        Camera3d::default(),
        bevy::camera::Hdr,
        SmokeCamera::HIGH, // the quality dial; HIGH is the default
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.7, -10.0).looking_at(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), Vec3::Y),
    ));
    // The directional light that lights the smoke.
    commands.spawn((
        DirectionalLight::default(),
        SmokeSun,
        Transform::from_xyz(-4.0, 10.0, -6.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y),
    ));
    // The level: smoke flows around every mesh marked SmokeObstacle. Include the floor.
    commands.spawn((
        Mesh3d(meshes.add(Plane3d::default().mesh().size(50.0, 50.0))),
        MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6))),
        SmokeObstacle,
    ));
    commands.spawn((
        Mesh3d(meshes.add(Cuboid::new(10.0, 3.0, 0.3))),
        MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.55))),
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.5, 6.0),
        SmokeObstacle,
    ));
    // A smoke grenade popping at the origin.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
}
```

- `SmokePlugin::default()` simulates in Y-up metres at 128 ticks a second with the default rules. `SmokePlugin { config }` takes other units and rules (recipe "Your own units").
- `SmokeCamera` goes on every `Camera3d` that should see volumetric or faceted smoke. Crystal smoke is plain meshes, which any camera draws.
- `SmokeSun` marks the light that lights volumetric and faceted smoke. With only one directional light it can be left out.
- `SmokeObstacle` meshes are voxelised in the background whenever one is added, moved or removed, and new smokes wait for the first level. With no level at all, smoke knows only a flat ground at height 0 and passes through walls.
- A `Smoke` pops where its entity is, and the entity despawns itself when the cloud is gone.
- HDR cameras (`bevy::camera::Hdr`) are recommended; LDR cameras get an approximate tonemap.

## Recipes

### A smoke grenade where it lands

Spawn the `Smoke` when the grenade comes to rest. The cloud pops at the entity's position on the current tick and stays there: moving the entity later doesn't move it. The entity despawns when the cloud is gone (after 18 s by default); despawning it sooner removes the cloud at once.

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Your game's message: a smoke grenade has come to rest.
#[derive(Message)]
struct GrenadeLanded {
    at: Vec3,
}

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_message::<GrenadeLanded>()
        .add_systems(Update, pop_grenades)
        .run();
}

fn pop_grenades(mut landed: MessageReader<GrenadeLanded>, mut commands: Commands) {
    for grenade in landed.read() {
        // A 90 m³ cloud. Its seed comes from its position, so the same throw gives
        // the same cloud on every machine.
        commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_translation(grenade.at)));
    }
}
```

For a grenade with a fuse, spawn the `Smoke` when it lands and set `config.tuning.timeline.start` to the fuse time: the fill then runs while the grenade sits there.

### Smoke walls, gas in a room, fog banks and steam

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_smokes(mut commands: Commands) {
    // A wall of smoke from the entity to 10 m along +X. Lasts 25 s.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::wall(Vec3::new(10.0, 0.0, 0.0)), Transform::from_xyz(-5.0, 0.3, 8.0)));
    // Poison gas filling a room 8 m × 3 m × 6 m: a box source centred on the entity,
    // with as much gas as the room holds. Walls marked SmokeObstacle keep it in.
    commands.spawn((
        Smoke::gas()
            .with_source(SmokeSource::Box {
                half_extents: Vec3::new(4.0, 1.5, 3.0),
            })
            .with_volume(8.0 * 3.0 * 6.0),
        Transform::from_xyz(14.0, 1.5, 18.0),
    ));
    // A fog bank fills a box for as long as its entity lives: despawn it to clear the fog.
    commands.spawn((Smoke::fog_bank(Vec3::new(6.0, 1.5, 4.0)), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.5, 20.0)));
    // Steam from a vent, as crystals, tinted.
    commands.spawn((
        Smoke::steam_vent()
            .with_style(SmokeStyle::Crystal)
            .with_tint(Color::srgb(0.9, 0.95, 1.0)),
        Transform::from_xyz(8.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    ));
}
```

Every preset takes the builders `with_style`, `with_volume`, `with_lifetime`, `with_grow_time`, `with_tint`, `with_seed` and `with_source` (`SmokeSource::Point`, `Line { offset }` or `Box { half_extents }`). Tint and `Smoke::density` are looks; the rest are rules.

A source must fit the cloud's fill grid: with the default tuning 14.4 m × 7.2 m × 14.4 m (48 × 24 × 48 voxels of 0.3 m), 1.8 m of it below the source. So a box's half extents can be at most 7.2 m across and 1.8 m up, a line at most 14.4 m along each axis, and a volume at most about 1,490 m³. Bigger ones are cut off at the grid's faces (the log says so): use several smokes, or a larger `Tuning::grid_dims` or `Tuning::voxel_size`.

### Bullets and explosions

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Forward your hitscan traces and explosions. Write the messages in Update (or anywhere
/// before SmokeSystems::Simulate, in PostUpdate): they land on the current tick.
fn forward_impacts(
    buttons: Res<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>,
    keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>,
    mut bullets: MessageWriter<SmokeBullet>,
    mut explosions: MessageWriter<SmokeExplosion>,
) {
    if buttons.just_pressed(MouseButton::Left) {
        // From the muzzle to what the shot hit: a tunnel that closes within about 2 s.
        bullets.write(SmokeBullet {
            start: Vec3::new(0.0, 1.6, -10.0),
            end: Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 10.0),
        });
    }
    if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::KeyH) {
        // An HE grenade: clears a sphere (3.5 m by default) that refills over about 5 s.
        explosions.write(SmokeExplosion {
            center: Vec3::new(0.0, 0.5, 3.0),
            radius: None,
        });
    }
}
```

Holes count in the rule: a tunnel opens a line of sight until it closes. `Tuning::holes` sets their sizes and times (`None` turns them off), and `Tuning::max_holes_per_cloud` (16) how many count per smoke, the newest first.

### Bot line of sight and muffled sound

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

#[derive(Component)]
struct Bot;

#[derive(Component)]
struct Enemy;

fn bot_vision(
    mut vision: SmokeVision,
    bots: Query<&GlobalTransform, With<Bot>>,
    enemies: Query<&GlobalTransform, With<Enemy>>,
) {
    for bot in &bots {
        let eye = bot.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.6, 0.0);
        for enemy in &enemies {
            let head = enemy.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.7, 0.0);
            // True once the line passes through Tuning::sight_threshold of cloud
            // (0.8 m by default), every smoke added up.
            if vision.blocks_sight(eye, head) {
                continue; // hidden by smoke
            }
            // The bot can see this enemy, unless something else is in the way.
        }
    }
}

/// How much of a sound gets through the smoke between its source and the listener.
fn muffle(mut vision: SmokeVision, listeners: Query<&GlobalTransform, With<Camera3d>>) {
    let source = Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 10.0);
    for ear in &listeners {
        let gain = vision.transmittance(source, ear.translation()); // 0..1
        let _ = gain; // feed it to your audio mixer
    }
}
```

`SmokeVision` answers for the current tick, in world units: `blocks_sight(a, b)`, `occlusion(a, b)` (the amount of cloud between two points), `transmittance(a, b)`, `density_at(p)` (every smoke added up) and `density_of(cloud, p)` (one smoke's). A server without Bevy asks `smokescreen::Smokes` the same questions and gets the same answers.

### Gas damage

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Your marker on the gas smokes you spawn:
/// `commands.spawn((Smoke::gas(), Gas, Transform::from_translation(at)))`.
#[derive(Component)]
struct Gas;

#[derive(Component)]
struct Health(f32);

fn gas_damage(
    mut vision: SmokeVision,
    gas: Query<&Smoke, With<Gas>>,
    mut players: Query<(&GlobalTransform, &mut Health)>,
    time: Res<Time>,
) {
    for (player, mut health) in &mut players {
        let chest = player.translation() + Vec3::new(0.0, 1.2, 0.0);
        // Only the gas smokes' density: plain smoke at the same spot does no harm.
        let density: f32 = gas
            .iter()
            .filter_map(Smoke::cloud) // a smoke's CloudId, once it has popped
            .map(|cloud| vision.density_of(cloud, chest))
            .sum();
        health.0 -= 25.0 * density * time.delta_secs();
    }
}
```

`density_of(cloud, p)` is one smoke's density at a point, 0..1: volumetric smoke's density, and 1 inside a crystal or faceted puff. `density_at(p)` adds up every smoke's, gas or not. Asked per smoke, damage can also say whose gas it was. A server on the core alone asks `view.density_of(id, p)`, with the `CloudId` that `Smokes::pop` returned.

### The level from meshes, boxes or your own physics

Mark meshes with `SmokeObstacle` (Setup), or build the level yourself and insert it before smokes pop: a cloud keeps the shape it filled with.

```rust,no_run
use std::sync::Arc;

use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn load_level(mut commands: Commands) {
    // Boxes, for blockouts and tests.
    let walls = BoxObstacles::new(vec![ObstacleBox::from_center_size(
        Vec3::new(0.0, 1.5, 6.0),
        Vec3::new(10.0, 3.0, 0.3),
    )]);
    // Voxelised once, at the tuning's voxel size (0.3 m by default): every fill is then bit
    // lookups, and the clouds come out exactly as the boxes alone would make them.
    let level = VoxelObstacles::from_level(Vec3::new(-50.0, -2.0, -50.0), Vec3::new(50.0, 12.0, 50.0), 0.3, &walls);
    commands.insert_resource(SmokeLevel(Arc::new(level)));
}

/// From your physics engine: is the box at `center`, `half` either side, blocked?
/// Also asked with a `half` of 0, as a point test.
fn level_from_physics(overlaps_box: impl Fn(Vec3, f32) -> bool) -> VoxelObstacles {
    VoxelObstacles::build(Vec3::new(-50.0, -2.0, -50.0), Vec3::new(50.0, 12.0, 50.0), 0.3, |center, half| {
        overlaps_box(center, half)
    })
}

/// Open ground on purpose: say so, and the log stops warning about a missing level.
fn open_ground(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.insert_resource(SmokeLevel(Arc::new(FlatGround::new(0.0, UpAxis::Y))));
}
```

For multiplayer, voxelise once and ship the voxels (`VoxelObstacles::to_bytes`, `VoxelObstacles::from_bytes`), so every machine has the same level. `VoxelObstacles::from_triangles` voxelises meshes outside Bevy.

### A glTF level

`SmokeObstacle` marks only its own entity's mesh, and a glTF scene's meshes are its descendants. Mark each one once the scene has spawned:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::world_serialization::WorldInstanceReady;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_level(mut commands: Commands, assets: Res<AssetServer>) {
    commands
        .spawn(WorldAssetRoot(assets.load("level.glb#Scene0")))
        .observe(mark_level_meshes);
}

fn mark_level_meshes(
    ready: On<WorldInstanceReady>,
    children: Query<&Children>,
    meshes: Query<(), With<Mesh3d>>,
    mut commands: Commands,
) {
    for entity in children.iter_descendants(ready.entity) {
        if meshes.contains(entity) {
            commands.entity(entity).insert(SmokeObstacle);
        }
    }
}
```

`GltfAssetLabel::Scene(0).from_asset("level.glb")` is the same path. Smokes that pop before the scene has spawned find no level: start throwing smoke once the level exists (`run_if(resource_exists::<SmokeLevel>)`). The meshes must keep their data in the main world, as the glTF loader does by default.

### The quality dial and budget mode

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn spawn_camera(mut commands: Commands) {
    // A fixed step: MINIMUM, LOWER, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH (the default) or ULTRA,
    // or any quality from 0 to 1 with SmokeCamera::with_quality(q).
    commands.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::MEDIUM));
}

/// The dial can change at any time, from a settings menu say.
fn set_quality(keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>, mut cameras: Query<&mut SmokeCamera>) {
    if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::F1) {
        for mut camera in &mut cameras {
            camera.quality = 1.0; // ultra
        }
    }
}

/// What the dial chose (SmokeQuality comes with SmokeCamera), and what it cost.
fn show_quality(cameras: Query<&SmokeQuality>) {
    for quality in &cameras {
        info!("smoke at {}: {:?} ms of GPU time", quality.tier_name(), quality.measured_ms);
    }
}
```

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::render::diagnostic::RenderDiagnosticsPlugin;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        // Budget mode needs GPU timings: RenderDiagnosticsPlugin, on a backend with
        // timestamp queries (Vulkan or DX12).
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, RenderDiagnosticsPlugin, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            // The best step that keeps this camera's smoke within 1.5 ms of GPU time.
            commands.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::budget(1.5)));
        })
        .run();
}
```

No step of the dial changes a cloud's shape, only how precisely it is drawn, so a player at a cheaper step doesn't see through smoke that hides them at a better one. (One exception: the experimental faceted look's see-through bullet tunnels come out a few pixels wider at cheaper steps.) Crystal smoke has no dial.

### Picking a look

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        // The look of smokes that don't choose their own, read at each pop, and the rest of the
        // look. SmokeSettings can change at any time; none of it changes what hides what.
        .insert_resource(SmokeSettings {
            style: SmokeStyle::Volumetric,
            noise_within_rule: NoiseWithinRule::Capped,
            ..default()
        })
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            // One smoke in another look.
            commands.spawn((
                Smoke::grenade().with_style(SmokeStyle::Crystal),
                Transform::from_xyz(4.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ));
        })
        .run();
}
```

- **Volumetric** (the default): soft and lit by the sun. On an Apple M4 at 1920×1080, one smoke adds 0.2 ms far away to 0.75 ms filling the screen, at the dial's best step. Its noise thins some smoke the rule counts, the same for every player. If a server, bots or abilities use the rule, set `noise_within_rule` to `Capped` (smoother inside, cheaper) or `Filled` (keeps the billows, costs more): then volumetric smoke at `Smoke::density` 1 or more never shows through what the rule blocks. (The gas, fog and steam presets draw thinner, at 0.5–0.6: a look only, so players see more through them than the rule allows.)
- **Crystal**: separate tumbling polyhedra drawn as ordinary meshes, about 0.1 ms. The cheapest to draw and to check. In a crystal-only game, `config.tuning.sight_threshold = 0.0` makes any contact block, and the picture and the rule then agree exactly.
- **Faceted**, experimental in 0.2: polyhedral puffs merged like metaballs. It costs 20–40 times what volumetric smoke costs to draw, and about 3 times more again with bullet tunnels.
- The style is a rule: every machine must give a smoke the same one, through `with_style` or the same `SmokeSettings::style`.

### Your own units (Z-up inches)

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::Config;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    // Everything the plugin takes or gives is now in Z-up inches: transforms, messages,
    // SmokeVision. Config::new converts the default rules (Tuning::new).
    let mut config = Config::new(Units::INCHES_Z_UP, 64.0);
    config.tuning.sight_threshold = 32.0; // 32 inches of cloud hide a player
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin { config }))
        .add_systems(Startup, |mut commands: Commands| {
            commands.spawn((
                Camera3d::default(),
                SmokeCamera::HIGH,
                Transform::from_xyz(0.0, -400.0, 64.0).looking_at(Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 40.0), Vec3::Z),
            ));
            commands.spawn((Smoke::grenade(), Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
        })
        .run();
}
```

Any other units: `Units::new(UpAxis::Z, metres_per_unit)`. The core works in metres internally and gives the same smoke in every unit system.

### Multiplayer in Bevy

When a server decides the smoke, drive the smoke's clock from your netcode and pop the clouds the server announces with their own ticks:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::CloudSpec;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

/// Stand-in for your netcode's state.
#[derive(Resource, Default)]
struct Net {
    server_tick: u64,
    interpolation_tick: u64,
    interpolation_fraction: f32,
    /// Pops the server announced: each spec carries its pop tick.
    pops: Vec<CloudSpec>,
    /// Shots the server announced: start, end and tick.
    bullets: Vec<(Vec3, Vec3, u64)>,
}

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, SmokePlugin::default()))
        .init_resource::<Net>()
        // The clock follows your netcode instead of Bevy's virtual time.
        .insert_resource(SmokeClock { auto: false, ..default() })
        .add_systems(Update, sync_smoke)
        .run();
}

fn sync_smoke(mut net: ResMut<Net>, mut clock: ResMut<SmokeClock>, mut world: ResMut<SmokeWorld>) {
    clock.tick = net.server_tick; // fills advance to it, and SmokeVision answers for it
    clock.draw_tick = Some(net.interpolation_tick); // the tick drawn
    clock.draw_fraction = net.interpolation_fraction; // how far the frame is past it
    // Events with their own ticks may arrive late or out of order: every machine
    // computes the same clouds from the same events.
    for spec in net.pops.drain(..) {
        world.pop(spec);
    }
    for (start, end, tick) in net.bullets.drain(..) {
        world.bullet(start, end, tick);
    }
}
```

- Send each pop's `CloudSpec` (origin, pop tick, seed, style, source, volume, timeline: a couple of dozen bytes; it has no serde, so send its fields) and each bullet and explosion with its tick.
- Every machine needs the same `Tuning` (in `SmokePlugin { config }`) and the same level: voxelise once and ship `VoxelObstacles::to_bytes`.
- `SmokeWorld` is the core's `Smokes` the plugin runs (it derefs to it). Clouds popped on it are drawn, with the default look (no tint), until they end or `world.remove(id)`. A `Smoke` entity pops on the current `SmokeClock::tick`, so it suits pops your own machine decides.
- A view of a recent past tick answers as it would have then (lag compensation): `world.view(tick).blocks_sight(a, b)`. Clouds and holes are kept for `Config::history_ticks` (a second by default) after they end.

### A first-person weapon inside smoke

Smoke is drawn over everything the world camera drew, a weapon half a metre from the eye included. Draw the weapon with a second camera after it, without `SmokeCamera`:

```rust,no_run
use bevy::camera::ClearColorConfig;
use bevy::camera::visibility::RenderLayers;
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_smokescreen::prelude::*;

const WEAPON_LAYER: usize = 1;

fn spawn_player(mut commands: Commands, mut meshes: ResMut<Assets<Mesh>>, mut materials: ResMut<Assets<StandardMaterial>>) {
    commands
        .spawn((Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 1.6, -3.5), Visibility::default()))
        .with_children(|player| {
            // The world camera: the level and the smoke.
            player.spawn((Camera3d::default(), SmokeCamera::HIGH));
            // The weapon camera: drawn after the world camera, over its picture, and only
            // the weapon's layer.
            player.spawn((
                Camera3d::default(),
                Camera {
                    order: 1,
                    clear_color: ClearColorConfig::None,
                    ..default()
                },
                RenderLayers::layer(WEAPON_LAYER),
            ));
            player.spawn((
                Mesh3d(meshes.add(Cuboid::new(0.08, 0.1, 0.6))),
                MeshMaterial3d(materials.add(Color::srgb(0.15, 0.15, 0.17))),
                Transform::from_xyz(0.22, -0.2, -0.45),
                RenderLayers::layer(WEAPON_LAYER),
            ));
        });
    // Light the world and the weapon.
    commands.spawn((
        DirectionalLight::default(),
        SmokeSun,
        RenderLayers::from_layers(&[0, WEAPON_LAYER]),
        Transform::from_xyz(-4.0, 10.0, -6.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y),
    ));
}
```

### A dedicated server on the core alone

```toml
[dependencies]
smokescreen = "0.2"
```

```rust
use smokescreen::glam::Vec3;
use smokescreen::*;

/// Your game's collision behind the Level trait, in your units: here boxes in Z-up
/// inches, as (min, max), on a floor at z = 0.
struct Brushes(Vec<(Vec3, Vec3)>);

impl Level for Brushes {
    /// Is the cube at `center`, `half` either side, blocked?
    fn is_blocked(&self, center: Vec3, half: f32) -> bool {
        center.z < half
            || self
                .0
                .iter()
                .any(|(lo, hi)| (center + half).cmpgt(*lo).all() && (center - half).cmplt(*hi).all())
    }

    /// Only renderers ask this, for lighting; a server never does.
    fn ray_hit(&self, _origin: Vec3, _dir: Vec3, _max_dist: f32) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

fn main() {
    // Your units and tick rate; the rules in those units.
    let mut config = Config::new(Units::INCHES_Z_UP, 64.0);
    config.tuning.sight_threshold = 32.0; // 32 inches of cloud hide a player
    let walls = Brushes(vec![(Vec3::new(-400.0, 300.0, 0.0), Vec3::new(400.0, 320.0, 160.0))]);
    let mut smokes = Smokes::new(config, walls);

    // Events from your game simulation, each with its tick.
    let origin = Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    smokes.pop(CloudSpec::new(origin, 0, CloudSpec::seed_from_origin(origin), Style::Volumetric));
    for tick in 0..=2 * 64 {
        smokes.advance(tick); // every tick: the fills spend their budget
    }
    // Two seconds later the cloud has grown: it hides one player from the other.
    let (eye, enemy) = (Vec3::new(-400.0, 0.0, 64.0), Vec3::new(400.0, 0.0, 64.0));
    let view = smokes.view(2 * 64); // Copy + Sync: share it between threads
    assert!(view.blocks_sight(eye, enemy));
    // A shot along the line opens a tunnel through the smoke for a while.
    smokes.bullet(eye, enemy, 2 * 64);
}
```

- A cloud at tick *t* is a pure function of its `CloudSpec`, the level, the `Tuning` and *t*, and holes are events with ticks: send them to clients, and every machine computes the same clouds. Events may arrive late or out of order, and late joiners catch up from the same events.
- `Level::is_inside(point)` defaults to `is_blocked(point, 0.0)`; override it if a box of size zero isn't a point test in your collision code.
- Or fill on the server only: `fill_cloud(&config, &spec, &level)` gives a `CloudShape` for the clients' `Smokes::insert`, with the same crate version at both ends.
- `Config::fill_budget` is the fill work per tick (about 0.2 ms on a small cloud VM, under 0.1 ms on an Apple M4). It grows only when a fill wouldn't otherwise be ready by the time its cloud starts, and the finished cloud is the same however the work is split.

## Gotchas

- **Compute shaders.** Volumetric and faceted smoke need them: native, or WebGPU in a browser (Bevy's `webgpu` feature, or `bevy_smokescreen`'s). On WebGL2 only crystal smoke is drawn, and the log says why.
- **Transparent objects behind smoke show through it.** Alpha-blended objects (tracers, muzzle-flash sprites, particles) behind or inside volumetric or faceted smoke draw over it at full strength: Bevy draws them after the smoke, which writes no depth. Opaque and `AlphaMode::Mask` objects are hidden properly, crystal smoke hides everything, and transparent objects in front of a smoke are fine. For effects that must stay hidden, use one of those, or hide them where `blocks_sight(camera, effect)`.
- **A first-person weapon needs its own camera** (recipe above), or smoke draws over it.
- **Orthographic cameras** draw no volumetric or faceted smoke; crystal smoke works.
- **Bevy 0.20 only.** `bevy_smokescreen` 0.1 and 0.2 are both for Bevy 0.20.
- **At most `Tuning::max_clouds` smokes count at once** (32): past that the oldest stop counting and aren't drawn, a long-lived fog bank first. At most 32 volumetric or faceted smokes are drawn at once; raise `max_clouds` past 32 only for crystal smoke.
- **The level comes first.** A cloud keeps the shape it filled with: closing a door doesn't re-shape a smoke, and clouds don't drift with wind.
- **Floors.** A single sheet facing up (a `Plane3d`) counts as ground, solid all the way down: use a box for a raised floor with air below it. Meshes need triangles facing outwards, as Bevy's shapes have; against inward-facing meshes and single upright sheets, smoke stops up to half a voxel short.
- **Mesh data must stay in the main world** for `SmokeObstacle` (the default; not `RenderAssetUsages::RENDER_WORLD` alone).
- **Lights.** Volumetric and faceted smoke take one directional light (`SmokeSun`) and up to 8 point lights, unshadowed; spot lights don't light them. Crystal smoke takes any light. A camera lit by an environment map or its own `AmbientLight` needs `SmokeSettings::ambient_override` set to match.
- **Faceted is experimental in 0.2**: costly to draw (see "Picking a look").
- **Safari 26** can't compile Bevy 0.20's `StandardMaterial` shader for meshes with UVs (Bevy's shader, not the smoke's): textured meshes need a fix in Bevy.

## Warnings the plugin logs

Each is logged once per app, with what to do. If a log shows one:

- "No active camera has SmokeCamera": add `SmokeCamera` to the `Camera3d` that should see smoke.
- "SmokeCamera is on an orthographic camera": use a perspective projection there, or crystal smoke.
- "The camera … has its own AmbientLight" or "… is lit by an environment map": set `SmokeSettings::ambient_override`.
- "SmokeCamera::budget_ms needs GPU timings": add `RenderDiagnosticsPlugin`, on Vulkan or DX12.
- "… directional lights have SmokeSun" or "… directional lights and none has SmokeSun": keep `SmokeSun` on exactly one.
- "A smoke popped with no level": mark the level's meshes, floor included, with `SmokeObstacle`, or insert a `SmokeLevel` before smokes pop; for open ground on purpose, `SmokeLevel(Arc::new(FlatGround::new(height, UpAxis::Y)))`.
- "A smoke's box source …", "A smoke's line source …" or "A smoke asks for a volume of …, more than its fill grid holds": a smaller source or several smokes, or a larger `grid_dims` or `voxel_size`.
- "A smoke popped inside solid level geometry": pop smokes in open air, on or just above the floor. If every smoke does this, check that the level's meshes face outwards.
- "More smokes are alive than Tuning::max_clouds": fewer at once, or a larger `max_clouds` (past 32, crystal smoke only).
- "More than 32 volumetric or faceted smokes count at once" or "Tuning::max_clouds is …, but at most 32 …": keep `max_clouds` at 32 or less, or use crystal smoke for the rest.
- "More than 512 holes are open in the smokes drawn": keep `max_holes_per_cloud` × the smokes drawn at once within 512.
- "SmokeObstacle is on an entity without a Mesh3d": put it on the mesh entities themselves (recipe "A glTF level").
- "A SmokeObstacle mesh … has no triangle data in the main world": use a triangle list, loaded with `RenderAssetUsages::MAIN_WORLD`.
- "A SmokeObstacle mesh failed to load": fix the asset, or take `SmokeObstacle` off that entity; smokes wait for the level until then.
- "SmokePlugin was added before Bevy's RenderPlugin" (or a panic that it needs Bevy's AssetPlugin): add it after `DefaultPlugins`.
- "The GPU device … offers no compute shaders": WebGL2; in a browser, build with WebGPU. Crystal smoke still works.

## API: bevy_smokescreen

In `bevy_smokescreen::prelude` unless marked "root".

- [SmokePlugin](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokePlugin.html): the plugin. `SmokePlugin::default()` or `SmokePlugin { config }`; add it after `DefaultPlugins`.
- [Smoke](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.Smoke.html): component, a cloud popping where its entity is. Presets `grenade()`, `wall(offset)`, `gas()`, `fog_bank(half_extents)`, `steam_vent()`; builders `with_style`, `with_volume`, `with_lifetime`, `with_grow_time`, `with_tint`, `with_seed`, `with_source`; fields `density`, `despawn_when_done`; `cloud()` gives its `CloudId` once popped (for `SmokeVision::density_of`).
- [SmokeSource](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeSource.html): `Point`, `Line { offset }`, `Box { half_extents }`.
- [SmokeStyle](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeStyle.html): `Volumetric` (the default), `Crystal`, `Faceted` (experimental). The core's `Style`.
- [SmokeCamera](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeCamera.html): component for each `Camera3d` that should see smoke, with its quality dial. `MINIMUM`, `LOWER`, `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` (the default), `ULTRA`, `with_quality(q)`, `budget(ms)`; fields `quality`, `budget_ms`, `temporal_jitter` (on with TAA), `measured_depth`, and `volumetric` and `facets` to pin the dial's knobs.
- [SmokeQuality](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/quality/struct.SmokeQuality.html): component that comes with `SmokeCamera`: what the dial chose. `tier`, `tier_name()`, `measured_ms`, `predicted_ms`.
- [SmokeSun](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeSun.html): marks the directional light that lights the smoke.
- [SmokeObstacle](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeObstacle.html): marks level meshes the smoke flows around.
- [SmokeLevel](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeLevel.html): resource, the level as any `Level`: `SmokeLevel(Arc::new(level))`. `SmokeObstacle` builds it, or insert your own.
- [SmokeBullet](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeBullet.html) and [SmokeExplosion](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeExplosion.html): messages, a tunnel along a shot (`start`, `end`) and a cleared sphere (`center`, `radius`).
- [SmokeVision](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeVision.html): system parameter for gameplay queries at the current tick: `blocks_sight(a, b)`, `occlusion(a, b)`, `transmittance(a, b)`, `density_at(p)`, `density_of(cloud, p)`, `tick()`.
- [SmokeSettings](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeSettings.html): resource, the look, which can change at any time: `style`, `extinction`, `albedo`, `noise_within_rule`, `ambient_override`, `wind`, `crystal_shadows`, the noise, and debug views.
- [NoiseWithinRule](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.NoiseWithinRule.html): `Off` (the default), `Capped`, `Filled`.
- [SmokeClock](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeClock.html): resource, the tick: `tick`, `draw_tick`, `draw_fraction`, `auto`.
- [SmokeWorld](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.SmokeWorld.html): resource, the core's `Smokes` the plugin runs (it derefs to it): pops, holes and queries at any tick.
- [SmokeSystems](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/enum.SmokeSystems.html): system sets in `PostUpdate`, after transform propagation: `Simulate`, then `PrepareRender`.
- [CrystalPuff](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/struct.CrystalPuff.html): marks the entities the plugin spawns for crystal puffs.
- [quality](https://docs.rs/bevy_smokescreen/0.2/bevy_smokescreen/quality/index.html): the dial's steps: `VolumetricQuality` and `FacetQuality` (the knobs at each step, to pin with `SmokeCamera::volumetric` and `facets`), `TIER_NAMES`. `SmokeResolution` is the fraction of the screen's resolution volumetric smoke is marched at.
- Root: `Config`, `Tuning`, `CloudSpec`, `CloudSource`, `CloudId`, `Smokes`, `Level`, `SmokeTimeline` (the core's `Timeline`), `HoleSettings`, `SharedLevel`, and the core itself as `bevy_smokescreen::smokescreen`.

## API: smokescreen

- [Smokes](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Smokes.html): the world of clouds. `new(config, level)`, `pop(spec)`, `bullet(start, end, tick)`, `explosion(center, radius, tick)`, `advance(tick)`, `view(tick)`, and `blocks_sight`, `occlusion`, `density_at`, `density_of` at a tick; `insert(spec, shape)`, `remove(id)`, `clear()`, `set_level(level)`, `clouds()`, `cloud(id)`, `pending_fills()`.
- [View](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.View.html): every cloud at one tick, `Copy + Sync`: `blocks_sight`, `occlusion`, `density_at`, `density_of`, `tick`. Allocates nothing.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Config.html): `Config::new(units, tick_rate)`; `tuning`, `fill_budget`, `level_query_units`, `history_ticks`, `cached_ticks`.
- [Tuning](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Tuning.html): the rules, the same on every machine. `Tuning::new(&units)`; `grid_dims`, `voxel_size`, `volume`, `up_cost`, `down_cost`, `lumpiness`, `lump_size`, `floor_fraction`, `timeline`, `facets`, `crystals`, `facet_rule`, `volume_steps`, `holes`, `max_holes_per_cloud`, `max_clouds`, `sight_threshold`.
- [CloudSpec](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudSpec.html): a pop, all a server has to send. `new(origin, pop_tick, seed, style)`, `with_source(source)`, `seed_from_origin(origin)`; fields `source`, `volume`, `timeline`.
- [CloudSource](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.CloudSource.html): `Point`, `Line { end }`, `Box { half_extents }`.
- [Style](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.Style.html): `Volumetric`, `Faceted` (experimental), `Crystal`.
- [Level](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/trait.Level.html): trait for level geometry: `is_blocked(center, half_extent)`, `ray_hit(origin, dir, max_dist)`, and `is_inside(point)`, which has a default.
- [FlatGround](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FlatGround.html), [BoxObstacles](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.BoxObstacles.html) with [ObstacleBox](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.ObstacleBox.html), and [VoxelObstacles](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.VoxelObstacles.html): ready-made levels. `VoxelObstacles::build`, `from_level`, `from_triangles`, `to_bytes`, `from_bytes`.
- [Units](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Units.html) and [UpAxis](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.UpAxis.html): `Units::METRES_Y_UP`, `Units::INCHES_Z_UP`, `Units::new(up, metres_per_unit)`.
- [Timeline](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.Timeline.html): a cloud's life in seconds: `start`, `grow_time`, `lifetime`, `fade_time`.
- [HoleSettings](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.HoleSettings.html): bullet tunnels' and explosions' sizes and times.
- [FacetSettings](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FacetSettings.html), [FacetRule](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.FacetRule.html) (`Exact`, `Chords`, `Core`), [FacetLimits](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.FacetLimits.html), [ShapeMix](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.ShapeMix.html), [Polyhedron](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.Polyhedron.html) and [VolumeSteps](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/enum.VolumeSteps.html) (`Voxel`, `HalfVoxel`): puff shapes, and how the rule counts faceted and volumetric clouds.
- [fill_cloud](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/fn.fill_cloud.html) and [CloudShape](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudShape.html): a fill on the server, sent to clients for `Smokes::insert`.
- [CloudId](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudId.html) and [CloudInfo](https://docs.rs/smokescreen/0.2/smokescreen/struct.CloudInfo.html): a cloud's handle (not shared between machines), and what `clouds()` and `cloud(id)` give: `id`, `spec`, `timeline`, `start_tick`, `end_tick`, `age`.
